survivors.evidence: patch_opf_fonts only appends manifest <item> entries for the embedded fonts (`new_items.append(f'<item id="{candidate}" href="{path}" media-type="{media_type}"/>')`) and never emits the Apple gate. The base epub_working/content.opf <package> (line 2: `<package xmlns="http://www.idpf.org/2007/opf" version="3.0" unique-identifier="uuid_id">`) carries NO `prefix="ibooks: ..."` and the <metadata> block (lines 3-21) has NO `<meta property="ibooks:specified-fonts">true</meta>`; there is no META-INF/com.apple.ibooks.display-options.xml (only container.xml exists). Grep across scripts/, content/editions.yaml and epub_working/ for `ibooks`/`specified-fonts`/`display-options` returns zero matches in any build input. Yet style_config.EMBED_FONT_PATHS is non-empty in EVERY edition (Cardo Latin/Greek/Hebrew + Noto Serif Ethiopic, lines 94-113), and these ARE shipped in v0.1.0. The build's largest_piece_kb stat is likewise informational (build_edition.py 5291). The test suite is no backstop either: tests/test_file_split.py:1003 only asserts `max(...) < len(text)` (smaller than the whole monolith), not bounded to target.

Read piece bytes via zf.getinfo(n).file_size, not len(decoded text). Mirror it as a per-piece assertion in test_file_split so a regression fails in CI, not only on device.

Add an oversized-piece gate that reads TRUE uncompressed bytes and sits above the legitimate over-cap single-chapter regime, in two places:

    byte_sizes = {n: zf.getinfo(n).file_size for n in pieces}

(B) scripts/build_edition.py — promote the already-computed largest_piece_kb from a silent stat into a build-time WARN/FAIL so the regression is caught at build, not only post-hoc. survivors.title: updates.compare_versions ranks a pre-release (1.0.0-rc1 / 1.0.0a) as NEWER than the final release, inverting the documented intent
survivors.evidence: `_version_key` builds a tuple per component, so `_version_key("1.0.0")` = `((0,1),(0,0),(0,0))` and `_version_key("1.0.0-rc1")` = `((0,1),(0,0),(0,0),(1,'rc'),(0,1))`. survivors.title: SSRF allowlist is bypassable via HTTP redirects — http.get/put validate only the initial URL, then urllib follows 3xx to any host (reachable through the unauthenticated-by-default url_override route)

The module's stated posture — "a file:// URL can't bypass the host allowlist" / fail-closed egress — is defeated for any allowlisted host that can be made to redirect (e.g. `archive.org`, which hosts user-controllable content and open-redirect-prone paths). Same defect in `put()` (line 232/240).
survivors.fix: Disable redirect-following in the http module and validate any redirect target against the same allowlist before following. Alternatively set a handler that returns no redirect and have callers opt in explicitly. Fold both call sites (get + put) into the one fix.
